title.zh: 卷一百二十三 列傳第七十三: 劉晏 第五琦 班宏 班紹 李巽
title.en: Volume 123 Biographies 73: Liu Yan, Di Wuqi, Ban Hong, Ban Shao, Li Xun
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 列傳第七十三: 劉晏 第五琦 班宏 班紹 李巽 Volume 123 Biographies 73: Liu Yan, Di Wuqi, Ban Hong, Ban Shao, Li Xun

sentences.zh: 劉晏，字士安，曹州南華人。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Shi'an, was a native of Nanhua in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, styled Shi'an, came from Nanhua in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，舉神童，授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: At age seven he was recommended as a child prodigy and appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was nominated as a precocious youth and made Regular Scribe in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累授夏縣令，有能名。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Xia County and gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: After successive appointments as magistrate of Xia County, he became known for administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中侍御史，遷度支郎中、杭隴華三州刺史，尋遷河南尹。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Censor in the Palace, was promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenue, and became prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua; soon after he was transferred to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of palace attendant censor, then rose to vice director of the revenue bureau and prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua, and shortly afterward became Intendant of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 時史朝義盜據東都，寄理長水。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi was occupying the Eastern Capital by force, so he administered affairs from Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Chaoyi holding the Eastern Capital, Yan governed from Changshui as his provisional seat.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆尹，頃之，加戶部侍郎、兼御史中丞，判度支，委府事於司錄張群、杜亞，綜大體，議論號為稱職。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor; shortly thereafter he was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge of revenue; he entrusted administrative affairs to Clerks Zhang Qun and Du Ya, while he handled overall policy, and his deliberations were said to be competent.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Chang'an, he soon added the titles of vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with charge of the revenue bureau. He left routine office work to Zhang Qun and Du Ya as recorders while he kept the broad direction in hand, and contemporaries judged his policy judgments sound.

sentences.zh: 無何，為酷吏敬羽所構，貶通州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was framed by the harsh official Jing Yu and demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the notorious official Jing Yu engineered charges against him, and he was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 復入為京兆尹、戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve again as Metropolitan Governor and Vice Minister of Revenue, with charge of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Chang'an as metropolitan governor and vice minister of revenue, again supervising the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 時顏真卿以文學正直出為利州刺史，晏舉真卿自代為戶部，乃加國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Zhenqing, known for literary learning and uprightness, had been sent out as prefect of Lizhou; Yan recommended Zhenqing to succeed him in the Revenue Ministry, and Yan was additionally made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing, admired for scholarship and integrity, had been posted to Lizhou, Liu Yan proposed that Zhenqing succeed him at the Ministry of Revenue and was himself made chancellor of the national university in addition.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，遷吏部尚書、平章事，領度支鹽鐵轉運租庸使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and made Grand Councilor, while retaining his posts as Commissioner for Revenue, Salt, Iron, Transport, and the Corvée Tax.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 he became minister of civil appointments and chief minister, continuing to head the combined revenue, salt, iron, transport, and corvée administration.

sentences.zh: 坐與中官程元振交通，元振得罪，晏罷相，為太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was punished for associating with the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen; when Yuanzhen fell from power, Yan was removed from the chancellorship and made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Charged with ties to the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen, he lost the premiership when Yuanzhen was disgraced and was appointed mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 尋授御史大夫，領東都、河南、江淮、山南等道轉運租庸鹽鐵使如故。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and continued to hold his former posts as Transport Commissioner for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jianghuai, Shan'nan, and other circuits, as well as Commissioner for the Corvée Tax, Salt, and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made chief censor while keeping his transport and fiscal commissions over the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jianghuai, Shan'nan, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 時新承兵戈之後，中外艱食，京師米價鬥至一千，官廚無兼時之積，禁軍乏食，畿縣百姓乃挼穗以供之。

translations.literal: The dynasty had newly emerged from warfare; inside and outside the capital food was scarce; rice in the capital reached a thousand cash per dou; the government kitchens had no stores beyond a single meal; the palace guards lacked food; and the people of the capital districts pounded grain spikes by hand to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still recovering from war. Food was desperately short everywhere; in Chang'an a dou of rice cost a thousand cash. The imperial kitchens held barely one meal's reserve, the palace guards went hungry, and peasants in the suburbs threshed ears of grain by hand to feed them.

sentences.zh: 晏受命後，以轉運為己任，凡所經歷，必究利病之由。

translations.literal: After Yan received his mandate, he made transport his personal responsibility, and wherever he traveled he thoroughly investigated the causes of profit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Once charged with the task, Yan treated grain transport as his own mission and wherever he went traced every cause of waste or efficiency.

sentences.zh: 至江淮，以書遺元載曰：

translations.literal: When he reached the Jianghuai region, he sent a letter to Yuan Zai saying:
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jianghuai, he wrote Yuan Zai:

sentences.zh: 浮於淮、泗，達於汴，入於河，西循底柱、硤石、少華，楚帆越客，直抵建章、長樂，此安社稷之奇策也。

translations.literal: Floating on the Huai and Si, reaching Bian, entering the Yellow River, and proceeding west along Dizhu, Xiaoshi, and Shaohua—Chu sails and Yue merchants arriving straight at Jianzhang and Changle: this is the extraordinary stratagem to secure the state.
translations.idiomatic: Grain could float up the Huai and Si, reach Bian, enter the Yellow River, and run west past Dizhu, Xiaoshi, and Shaohua so that Chu and Yue shipping would berth straight at the imperial palaces—this was the bold plan to stabilize the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 晏賓於東朝，猶有官謗，相公終始故舊，不信流言，賈誼復召宣室，弘羊重興功利，敢不悉力以答所知。

translations.literal: Yan, though favored at the Eastern Court, still bore official slander; the Chancellor had been my friend from first to last—do not believe wandering rumors; Jia Yi was summoned again to the Xuan Chamber, and Sang Hongyang revived profit and utility—how dare I not exert every effort to repay one who knows me?
translations.idiomatic: Though I still face court gossip, you have known me from the first as an old colleague and will not heed idle talk. Just as Jia Yi was called back to the privy chamber and Sang Hongyang was trusted again to manage state revenue, I dare not spare myself in repaying your confidence.

sentences.zh: 驅馬陜郊，見三門渠津遺跡。

translations.literal: Riding through the Shaan suburbs, I saw the vestiges of the canals and crossings at Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling through the lands west of Shan, I found the remains of the Sanmen canal works.

sentences.zh: 到河陰、鞏、洛，見宇文愷置梁公堰，分黃河水入通濟渠；

translations.literal: At Heyin, Gong, and Luo I saw how Yuwen Kai had built the Duke of Liang's weir to divide the Yellow River into the Tongji Canal;
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin, Gong, and Luoyang I inspected Yuwen Kai's weir diverting Yellow River water into the Tongji Canal;

sentences.zh: 大夫李傑新堤故事，飾像河廟，凜然如生。

translations.literal: and the story of Supervisor Li Jie's new embankment, with statues adorned at the River Temple, stern as though living.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Jie's later embankment, with life-like images set up at the River God shrine.

sentences.zh: 涉滎郊、浚澤，遙瞻淮甸，步步探討，知昔人用心，則潭、衡、桂陽必多積谷，關輔汲汲，只緣兵糧。

translations.literal: Crossing the Song suburbs and dredging marshes, gazing from afar at the Huai district, investigating step by step—I knew how our predecessors applied their minds: Tan, Heng, and Guiyang surely store abundant grain; the Guanzhong region strains only because of military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the Song riverland and dredging the marshes, scanning the Huai plain at every turn, I saw why the ancients labored as they did: the lake districts around Tan, Heng, and Guiyang must hold huge reserves, while Guanzhong starves chiefly for want of army rations.

sentences.zh: 漕引瀟、湘、洞庭，萬里幾日，淪波卦席，西指長安。

translations.literal: Transport by water from the Xiao and Xiang and Dongting—in a few days over ten thousand li—the waves rolling like mat patterns on deck, pointing west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Once grain is floated down the Xiao, the Xiang, and Dongting Lake, ten thousand li can be covered in days, with sails quartering the waves all the way west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 三秦之人，待此而飽；

translations.literal: The people of the Three Qins will rely on this to be fed;
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Three Qin regions would at last eat their fill;

sentences.zh: 六軍之眾，待此而強。

translations.literal: the masses of the Six Armies will rely on this to be strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial armies would grow strong on it.

sentences.zh: 天子無側席之憂，都人見泛舟之役；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven will have no worry of sitting sideways on his mat; the capital populace will see boats passing to and fro;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would no longer fret from hunger, and the capital would see grain boats plying the canals again;

sentences.zh: 四方旅拒者可以破膽，三河流離者於茲請命。

translations.literal: those who resist from the four quarters can have their courage broken; those displaced along the Three Rivers can here plead for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: rebels in the provinces would lose heart, and refugees along the Yellow, Huai, and other rivers could beg for relief.

sentences.zh: 相公匡戴明主，為富人侯，此今之切務，不可失也。

translations.literal: The Chancellor aids and supports the enlightened sovereign and becomes a marquis among wealthy men—this is today's urgent task and must not be missed.
translations.idiomatic: By supporting our enlightened sovereign you would become a great lord of wealth—this is the urgent task of the moment and must not be let slip.

sentences.zh: 使仆湔洗瑕穢，率罄愚懦，當憑經義，請護河堤，冥勤在官，不辭水死。

translations.literal: Enable this servant to wash away stains, lead with all my foolish timidity, rely on canonical principles, request to guard the river dikes, labor in office in obscurity, and not refuse death by water.
translations.idiomatic: Give me leave to clear my name and give all my poor wits to the cause. On principle I ask to defend the river works myself, to labor at my post in silence, and not to shirk death by drowning.

sentences.zh: 然運之利病，各有四五焉。

translations.literal: Yet the profit and harm of transport each have four or five aspects.
translations.idiomatic: Yet transport has its own four or five advantages and as many drawbacks.

sentences.zh: 晏自尹京入為計相，共五年矣。

translations.literal: Yan, from governing the capital to becoming chief of finance, has served five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: I have been metropolitan governor and then chief fiscal officer for five years altogether.

sentences.zh: 京師三輔百姓，唯苦稅畝傷多，若使江、湖米來每年三二十萬，即頓減徭賦，歌舞皇澤，其利一也。

translations.literal: The people of the capital and the Three Adjuncts suffer only from excessive land tax; if two or three hundred thousand piculs of grain from the rivers and lakes came each year, corvée and levies would be sharply reduced and they would sing of the sovereign's grace—this is the first benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The people around Chang'an groan under heavy land taxes; if two or three hundred thousand piculs of Jianghu grain arrived yearly, levies could drop at once and they would praise the throne's bounty—that is the first gain.

sentences.zh: 東都殘毀，百無一存。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital lies in ruins; not one part in a hundred remains.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital is in ruins; scarcely one building in a hundred still stands.

sentences.zh: 若米運流通，則饑人皆附，村落邑厘，從此滋多。

translations.literal: If grain transport flows freely, the hungry will all gather, and villages and hamlets will multiply from this.
translations.idiomatic: If grain shipping revives, starving refugees will settle there and hamlets will spring up again.

sentences.zh: 受命之日引海陵之倉以食鞏、洛，是計之得者，其利二也。

translations.literal: From the day of my mandate I have drawn on the granaries of Hailing to feed Gong and Luo—this is a sound plan; that is the second benefit.
translations.idiomatic: From the day I took office I have drawn Hailing's stores to feed Gong and Luoyang—a sound plan and the second gain.

sentences.zh: 諸將有在邊者，諸戎有侵敗王略者，或聞三江、五湖，貢輸紅粒，雲帆桂楫，輸納帝鄉，軍誌曰：「先聲後實，可以震耀夷夏。」

translations.literal: Generals stationed on the frontier and barbarians who encroach on the imperial domain—when they hear that from the Three Rivers and Five Lakes red grain is presented in tribute, with cloudlike sails and cassia oars shipping it to the imperial capital, military doctrine says: 'Sound precedes substance; this can awe barbarians and Chinese alike.'
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals and tribes that raid the borders, hearing that red grain from the Yangzi lakes is shipped on cloud-white sails and cassia-prowed boats to the capital, will recall the maxim that reputation should precede force—thus aweing both barbarian and Chinese.'

sentences.zh: 其利三也。

translations.literal: That is the third benefit.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third gain.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王之盛，皆云書同文，車同軌，日月所照，莫不率俾。

translations.literal: From antiquity the glory of emperors has been described as identical script and identical wheel-gauge, and all beneath the sun and moon submitting in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the height of imperial power has been described as one script, one track, and universal submission to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今舟車既通，商賈往來，百貨雜集，航海梯山，聖神輝光，漸近貞觀、永徽之盛，其利四也。

translations.literal: Now that boats and carts are connected, merchants come and go, goods of every kind gather, and trade crosses seas and mountains—the sage sovereign's radiance approaches the splendor of Zhenguan and Yonghui; that is the fourth benefit.
translations.idiomatic: With waterways and roads open again, merchants travel freely, goods pile up, and trade spans sea and mountain—the court's glory would approach the prosperity of the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras; that is the fourth gain.

sentences.zh: 所可疑者，函、陜雕殘，東周尤甚。

translations.literal: What gives pause is that Hangu and Shaan are carved to ruin, and the Eastern Zhou region is worst of all.
translations.idiomatic: What gives pause is the devastation of Hangu Pass and Shaan, worst of all in the old Eastern Zhou heartland.

sentences.zh: 過宜陽、熊耳，至武牢、成臯，五百里中，編戶千余而已。

translations.literal: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, within five hundred li there are only a little over a thousand registered households.
translations.idiomatic: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, five hundred li hold barely a thousand registered households.

sentences.zh: 居無尺椽，人無煙爨，蕭條淒慘，獸遊鬼哭。

translations.literal: Homes lack a single rafter; people lack cooking smoke; desolation is bleak and beasts roam while ghosts seem to wail.
translations.idiomatic: Not a rafter stands, no hearth smoke rises; the land is desolate, beasts roam, and it seems ghosts wail.

sentences.zh: 牛必羸角，輿必說輹，棧車輓漕，亦不易求。

translations.literal: Oxen are sure to be scrawny-horned, carts sure to have wheels come loose; even plank carts for haulage are not easily found.
translations.idiomatic: Oxen are emaciated, cart wheels fall off, and even simple haulage carts are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 今於無人之境，興此勞人之運，固難就矣，其病一也。

translations.literal: To launch this labor-consuming transport in a land without people is inherently hard to accomplish—that is the first drawback.
translations.idiomatic: To launch this laborious transport through uninhabited country is bound to fail—that is the first drawback.

sentences.zh: 河、汴有初，不修則毀澱，故每年正月發近縣丁男，塞長茭，決沮淤，清明桃花已後，遠水自然安流，陽侯、宓妃，不復太息。

translations.literal: The Yellow River and Bian Canal had their beginnings; if not maintained they silt up, so every first month conscript labor from nearby counties blocks long reeds and clears sediment; after Qingming and the peach blossoms, distant waters flow smoothly of themselves, and the River Lord and Lady Mi need sigh no more.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River and Bian Canal must be dredged yearly or they silt shut; each New Year laborers from nearby counties clear reeds and sediment, and after Qingming the distant reaches run clear again without the river gods' lament.

sentences.zh: 頃因寇難，總不掏拓，澤滅水，岸石崩，役夫需於沙，津吏旋於濘，千里洄上，罔水舟行，其病二也。

translations.literal: Recently because of rebellion dredging has altogether ceased; marshes have swallowed the water, bank stones have collapsed, laborers wait on sandbars, ferry clerks turn in the mud, and for a thousand li upstream there is no water for boats—that is the second drawback.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellions dredging has stopped entirely; marshes have swallowed the channel, banks have collapsed, laborers wait on sandbars, clerks flounder in mud, and for a thousand li upstream boats cannot sail—that is the second drawback.

sentences.zh: 東垣、底柱，澠池、二陵，北河運處五六百里，戍卒久絕，縣吏空拳。

translations.literal: From Dongyuan and Dizhu to Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li along the northern river transport route—garrison troops have long been cut off and county clerks are empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: From Dongyuan and Dizhu to Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li of the northern transport route have no garrisons left and county officials are powerless.

sentences.zh: 奪攘奸宄，窟穴囊橐。

translations.literal: Robbers and villains plunder and nest in caves with their loot.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and outlaws raid and hide in caves with their plunder.

sentences.zh: 夾河為藪，豺狼狺狺，舟行所經，寇亦能往，其病三也。

translations.literal: Along the river are marshes; wolves and jackals snarl; wherever boats pass, bandits can also go—that is the third drawback.
translations.idiomatic: Marshes line the river, wolves howl, and wherever boats can go bandits can follow—that is the third drawback.

sentences.zh: 東自淮陰，西臨蒲阪，亙三千里，屯戍相望。

translations.literal: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, spanning three thousand li, garrisons face one another.
translations.idiomatic: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, three thousand li of garrisons stand face to face.

sentences.zh: 中軍皆鼎司元侯，賤卒儀同青紫，每雲食半菽，又雲無挾纊，輓漕所至，船到便留，即非單車使折簡書所能制矣，其病四也。

translations.literal: Central Army posts are held by chief ministers and great marquises; lowly soldiers dress like the purple-clad elite; they always say they eat half beans and have no padded coats; wherever transport grain arrives, boats are detained on arrival—this is not something a lone envoy with a letter can control; that is the fourth drawback.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army posts are held by chief ministers and great lords; common soldiers dress like officers; they claim to eat half rations and lack winter coats; wherever grain convoys arrive the boats are seized on the spot—not something a lone commissioner with a letter can restrain—that is the fourth drawback.

sentences.zh: 惟小子畢其慮奔走之，惟中書詳其利病裁成之。

translations.literal: Only this humble servant will exhaust his thought and run about it; only the Secretariat will weigh profit and harm and complete the plan.
translations.idiomatic: I alone will give all my thought and effort to the task; only the Secretariat can weigh the pros and cons and bring the plan to completion.

sentences.zh: 晏累年已來，事缺名毀，聖慈含育，特賜生全。

translations.literal: Yan for many years has had his duties cut short and his name slandered; the sage's compassion nurtured him and specially granted him life.
translations.idiomatic: For years my duties were curtailed and my name slandered; the emperor's mercy spared my life.

sentences.zh: 月余家居，遽即臨遣，恩榮感切，思殞百身。

translations.literal: After a month at home he was suddenly sent on imperial mission; moved by grace and honor, he wished to die a hundred deaths in return.
translations.idiomatic: After barely a month at home I was suddenly dispatched on imperial business; overwhelmed by grace, I would gladly die a hundred deaths in return.

sentences.zh: 見一水不通，願荷鍤而先往；

translations.literal: seeing one waterway blocked, he wished to shoulder a spade and go first;
translations.idiomatic: Wherever a channel was blocked I wished to take a spade and go first;

sentences.zh: 見一粒不運，願負米而先趨。

translations.literal: seeing one grain not transported, he wished to carry rice and hurry ahead.
translations.idiomatic: wherever a grain was not moved I wished to carry rice and hurry ahead.

sentences.zh: 焦心苦形，期報明主，丹誠未克，漕引多虞，屏營中流，掩泣獻狀。

translations.literal: He tormented heart and body, hoping to repay the enlightened sovereign; his red sincerity had not yet succeeded, and grain transport had many worries; pacing anxiously midstream, he wept as he presented his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I wore myself out in body and mind to repay my sovereign; my loyal effort had not yet succeeded and transport still faced many perils; pacing midstream in anxiety, I wept as I submitted this memorial.

sentences.zh: 自此每歲運米數十萬石以濟關中。

translations.literal: From this time each year several hundred thousand piculs of grain were transported to relieve Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on several hundred thousand piculs of grain were shipped yearly to supply Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 又至德初，為國用不足，令第五琦於諸道榷鹽以助軍用，及晏代其任，法益精密，官無遺利。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of Zhide, because state revenue was insufficient, Di Wuqi was ordered to monopolize salt in the various circuits to aid military expenses; when Yan succeeded to his post, the law grew more precise and the government left no profit uncollected.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era, with state funds short, Di Wuqi was ordered to monopolize salt in the circuits for military expenses; when Yan took over, the system grew more precise and the treasury left no revenue uncollected.

sentences.zh: 初，歲入錢六十萬貫，季年所入逾十倍，而人無厭苦。

translations.literal: At first annual intake was six hundred thousand strings of cash; in later years intake exceeded ten times that, yet the people felt no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: At first annual revenue was six hundred thousand strings of cash; in later years it exceeded ten times that, yet the people bore no bitterness.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，通計一歲征賦所入總一千二百萬貫，而鹽利且過半。

translations.literal: By the end of Dali, total annual tax and levy intake amounted to twelve million strings of cash, and salt profits alone exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Dali era, total annual tax revenue reached twelve million strings of cash, with salt profits alone exceeding half.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年六月，與右僕射裴遵慶同赴本曹視事，敕尚食增置儲供，許內侍魚朝恩及宰臣已下常朝官鹹詣省送上。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Dali, together with Right Vice Director Pei Zunqing he went to his ministry to assume duties; an edict ordered the Imperial Kitchen to increase provisions, and allowed Eunuch Yu Chaoen and all regular court officials down to the chancellors to come to the ministry to present congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In June 769 he and Right Vice Director Pei Zunqing took up office at the Ministry of Personnel; the emperor ordered extra provisions from the imperial kitchen and allowed Eunuch Yu Chaoen and all regular court officials down to the chancellors to visit the ministry with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 八年，知三銓選事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he took charge of selection affairs in all three boards.
translations.idiomatic: In 773 he took charge of appointments in all three selection boards.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，誅宰臣元載，晏奉詔訊鞫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year the chancellor Yuan Zai was executed; Yan received an edict to interrogate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: In March 777 Chancellor Yuan Zai was executed; Yan was ordered to conduct the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 晏以載居任樹黨，布於天下，不敢專斷，請他官共事。

translations.literal: Yan, because Zai during his tenure had built factions spread throughout the realm, did not dare decide alone and requested other officials to join the case.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zai had built a faction network across the empire during his tenure, Yan did not dare decide alone and asked other officials to join the investigation.

sentences.zh: 敕御史大夫李涵、右散騎常侍蕭昕、兵部侍郎袁傪、禮部侍郎常袞、諫議大夫杜亞同推，載皆款伏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Officer Du Ya to join the inquiry; Zai confessed to all charges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Censor Li Han, Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Officer Du Ya to join the inquiry; Zai confessed to all charges.

sentences.zh: 初，晏承旨，門下侍郎、同平章事王縉亦處極法，晏謂涵等曰：重刑再覆，國之常典，況誅大臣，得不覆奏？

translations.literal: At first, when Yan received the imperial directive, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor Wang Jin was also to receive the extreme penalty; Yan said to Han and the others: 'Heavy punishments require double review—this is the state's constant rule; moreover, in executing a great minister, must we not report back for confirmation?'
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first received the order, Vice Director Wang Jin was also slated for execution; Yan told Han and the others: 'Heavy sentences require double review—that is state law; in executing a great minister, must we not report back for confirmation?'

sentences.zh: 又法有首從，二人同刑，亦宜重取進止。」

translations.literal: 'Moreover the law distinguishes principal and accomplice; when two men share the same sentence, we should also seek renewed imperial decision.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The law also distinguishes principal and accomplice; when two men face the same sentence, we should seek the throne's decision again.'

sentences.zh: 涵等從命。

translations.literal: Han and the others obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Han and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 及晏等覆奏，代宗乃減縉罪從輕。

translations.literal: When Yan and the others reported back, Emperor Daizong reduced Jin's crime to a lighter punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and the others reported back, Emperor Daizong lightened Jin's sentence.

sentences.zh: 縉之生，晏平反之力也。

translations.literal: That Jin lived was due to Yan's effort to reverse the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Jin owed his life to Yan's intervention.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In December 778 he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣常袞專政，以晏久掌銓衡，時議平允，兼司儲蓄，職舉功深，慮公望日崇，上心有屬。

translations.literal: At that time Chancellor Chang Gun monopolized government; because Yan had long controlled personnel selection, public opinion deemed him fair, and he also managed storage—his duties were fulfilled and his achievements deep; Gun feared Yan's public standing rising daily and that the sovereign's heart might turn to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chang Gun then dominated the court. Yan had long controlled appointments with a reputation for fairness and also managed state granaries with deep achievement; Gun feared Yan's rising prestige and that the emperor might favor him for higher office.

sentences.zh: 竊忌之，乃奏晏朝廷舊德，宜為百吏師長，外示崇重，內實去其權。

translations.literal: Secretly jealous, he memorialized that Yan was an old merit of the court and should be moral teacher to all officials—outwardly showing honor while inwardly stripping his power.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly jealous, he memorialized that Yan, a veteran of the court, should be mentor to all officials—honoring him in name while stripping his real authority.

sentences.zh: 及奏上，以晏使務方理，代其任者難其人，使務、知三銓並如故。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, because Yan's commission affairs were still being managed and no replacement could be found, his commission duties and charge of the three selection boards remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, because Yan's fiscal duties were still in order and no replacement could be found, his transport commission and control of the three selection boards remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜之亂也，河南節帥所據，多不奉法令，征賦亦隨之；

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Li Lingyao, the military governors holding Henan mostly did not obey laws and edicts, and tax collection followed suit;
translations.idiomatic: During Li Lingyao's rebellion the Henan military governors mostly ignored imperial law, and tax collection suffered likewise;

sentences.zh: 州縣雖益減，晏以羨余相補，人不加賦，所入仍舊，議者稱其能。

translations.literal: though prefectures and counties were further reduced, Yan used surplus revenue to compensate so the people were not charged extra levies and intake remained as before; commentators praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: though local revenues fell further, Yan used surpluses to make up the shortfall so the people paid no extra levies and state intake held steady; observers praised his skill.

sentences.zh: 自諸道巡院距京師，重價募疾足，置遞相望，四方物價之上下，雖極遠不四五日知，故食貨之重輕，盡權在掌握，朝廷獲美利而天下無甚貴甚賤之憂，得其術矣。

translations.literal: From the circuit inspection offices to the capital he paid high prices to recruit swift runners and set relay stations in sight of one another; the rise and fall of prices in the four quarters, however remote, was known within four or five days; thus the weight of grain and goods lay entirely in his grasp—the court gained fine profit while the realm had no fear of extreme dearth or cheapness; he had mastered the method.
translations.idiomatic: From his circuit inspection offices to the capital he hired swift couriers at high pay and set relay stations in chains; price movements even in the remotest regions were known within four or five days. He thus controlled the weight of grain and goods—the court gained handsome profit while the realm avoided extreme inflation or collapse; he had mastered the art.

sentences.zh: 凡所任使，多收後進有幹能者。

translations.literal: In all appointments he mostly recruited younger men of ability and competence.
translations.idiomatic: In appointments he mostly favored capable younger men.

sentences.zh: 其所總領，務乎急促，趨利者化之，遂以成風。

translations.literal: What he oversaw stressed urgency; those who sought profit were transformed by him, and this became the prevailing style.
translations.idiomatic: His departments stressed speed and efficiency; profit-seekers took his example until it became the prevailing style.

sentences.zh: 當時權勢，或以親戚為托，晏亦應之，俸給之多少，命官之遲速，必如其誌，然未嘗得親職事。

translations.literal: Powerful men of the time sometimes asked favors for relatives; Yan also complied—the amount of salary and the speed of appointment always matched their wishes, yet they never obtained substantive duties.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful men sometimes asked favors for relatives; Yan complied on salary and appointment timing as they wished, yet never gave them substantive duties.

sentences.zh: 其所領要務，必一時之選，故晏沒後二十余年，韓洄、元琇、裴腆、包佶、盧征、李衡繼掌財賦，皆晏故吏。

translations.literal: For key duties under his charge he always chose men of the moment; thus more than twenty years after Yan's death Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng successively managed fiscal affairs—all were Yan's former subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: For key posts he always chose the best men of the day; more than twenty years after his death Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng in turn ran fiscal affairs—all his former subordinates.

sentences.zh: 其部吏居數千里之外，奉教令如在目前，雖寢興宴語，而無欺紿，四方動靜，莫不先知，事有可賀者，必先上章奏。

translations.literal: His subordinates, though thousands of li away, obeyed orders as if before his eyes; even in sleep, rising, feasting, or conversation there was no deception; movements in the four quarters were all known to him first; when something merited congratulation, a memorial was always submitted first.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates thousands of li away obeyed his orders as if he stood before them; even in private moments there was no deceit. He learned of events across the empire before anyone else, and good news was always reported to the throne first.

sentences.zh: 江淮茶、橘，晏與本道觀察使各歲貢之，皆欲其先至。

translations.literal: Tea and oranges from Jianghuai—Yan and the circuit observation commissioners each presented them yearly as tribute, all wanting theirs to arrive first.
translations.idiomatic: Jianghuai tea and oranges were presented yearly as tribute by Yan and the circuit commissioners alike, each vying to arrive first.

sentences.zh: 有土之官，或封山斷道，禁前發者，晏厚以財力致之，常先他司，由是甚不為籓鎮所便。

translations.literal: Local officials sometimes sealed mountains and blocked roads to forbid early dispatch; Yan used ample funds to secure delivery and usually arrived before other offices—hence he was greatly disliked by the military governors.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials sometimes blocked roads to prevent early shipment; Yan used ample funds to secure delivery and usually beat other offices—making him deeply unpopular with the military governors.

sentences.zh: 晏理家以儉約稱，而重交敦舊，頗以財貨遺天下名土，故人多稱之。

translations.literal: Yan managed his household with a reputation for frugality, yet valued friendship and old ties and often gave wealth to famous scholars of the realm; therefore many praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ran his household frugally but valued old friendships and often gave money to famous scholars; many spoke well of him for it.

sentences.zh: 善訓諸子，鹹有學藝。

translations.literal: He trained his sons well; all had learning and arts.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his sons well; all were accomplished scholars.

sentences.zh: 任事十余年，權勢之重，鄰於宰相，要官重職，頗出其門。

translations.literal: In office more than ten years, his power and influence neared that of a chancellor; many key posts and heavy offices came from his faction.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years in office his power rivaled a chancellor's; many key posts went to his protégés.

sentences.zh: 既有材力，視事敏速，乘機無滯，然多任數，挾權貴，固恩澤，有口者必利啖之。

translations.literal: He had both talent and force, handled affairs swiftly, seized opportunities without delay; yet he often relied on stratagem, leveraged the powerful, secured favor and grace, and anyone with a voice he surely fed with profit.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and energetic, he handled affairs swiftly and seized every opportunity; yet he often used stratagem, leveraged the powerful, secured imperial favor, and bribed anyone who could speak for him.

sentences.zh: 當大歷時，事貴因循，軍國之用，皆仰於晏，未嘗檢轄。

translations.literal: During the Dali era affairs valued routine compliance; military and state expenses all depended on Yan, and no one ever audited him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era the court valued routine; military and state expenses all depended on Yan, and no one ever audited him.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，言事者稱轉運可罷多矣。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, memorialists often said grain transport could be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, many memorialists urged abolishing the transport commission.

sentences.zh: 初，楊炎為吏部侍郎，晏為尚書，各恃權使氣，兩不相得。

translations.literal: At first Yang Yan was Vice Minister of Personnel and Yan was Minister; each relied on power and threw his weight about; the two did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Yan was vice minister of personnel while Yan was minister; each abused his power and the two could not abide each other.

sentences.zh: 炎坐元載貶，晏快之，昌言於朝。

translations.literal: When Yang was demoted because of Yuan Zai, Yan rejoiced and spoke openly at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang was demoted over Yuan Zai's case, Yan rejoiced and spoke openly at court.

sentences.zh: 及炎入相，追怒前事，且以晏與元載隙憾，時人言載之得罪，晏有力焉。

translations.literal: When Yang entered the chancellorship he pursued old grievances, and because Yan had enmity with Yuan Zai, people of the time said Yan had had a hand in Zai's downfall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang became chancellor he pursued old grievances, and because Yan had feuded with Yuan Zai, contemporaries said Yan had helped bring Zai down.

sentences.zh: 炎將為載復仇，又時人風言代宗寵獨孤妃而又愛其子韓王迥，晏密啟請立獨孤為皇后。

translations.literal: Yang was about to avenge Zai, and moreover rumor said Emperor Daizong favored Consort Dugu and also loved her son, Prince Han Huai; Yan had secretly memorialized asking that Dugu be made empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yang meant to avenge Zai, and rumor held that Daizong favored Consort Dugu and loved her son Prince Han Huai; Yan had secretly urged making Dugu empress.

sentences.zh: 炎因對易攵流涕奏言：「賴祖宗福祐，先皇與陛下不為賊臣所間。

translations.literal: Yang, taking advantage of an audience, tearfully memorialized: 'Thanks to the ancestors' blessing, the late emperor and Your Majesty were not estranged by treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yang seized an audience to declare tearfully: 'Thanks to our ancestors' blessing, the late emperor and Your Majesty were not estranged by treacherous ministers.

sentences.zh: 不然，劉晏、黎幹之輩，搖動社稷，兇謀果矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise men like Liu Yan and Li Gan would have shaken the altars of state and their wicked plot would have succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise men like Liu Yan and Li Gan would have shaken the throne and their wicked plot would have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今幹以伏罪，晏猶領權，臣為宰相，不能正持此事，罪當萬死。」

translations.literal: Now Gan has confessed his crime, yet Yan still holds power; I as chancellor cannot rectify this matter—I deserve death ten thousand times.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gan has been punished, yet Yan still holds power; as chancellor I cannot rectify this—I deserve death ten thousand times.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫奏言：「此事曖昧，陛下以廓然大赦，不當究尋虛語。」

translations.literal: Cui Youfu memorialized: "This matter is vague; Your Majesty has proclaimed a broad amnesty and should not pursue empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu replied: "This matter is vague; Your Majesty has proclaimed a broad amnesty and should not pursue idle rumor."

sentences.zh: 硃泚、崔寧又從傍與祐甫救解之，寧言頗切，炎大怒，故斥寧令出鎮鄜坊以摧挫之。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also joined Youfu from the side in mediation; Ning's words were rather sharp; Yang was greatly angered and therefore expelled Ning to command Bin and Fang circuits to break his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also sided with Youfu; Ning spoke sharply; Yang was furious and banished Ning to command the Bin-Fang region to break his spirit.

sentences.zh: 遂罷晏轉運等使，尋貶為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan's posts as transport commissioner and the like were abolished; soon after he was demoted to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was stripped of his transport commissioner posts and, before long, demoted to prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 炎欲誣構其罪，知庾準與晏素有隙，舉為荊南節度，以伺晏動靜。

translations.literal: Yan wished to fabricate crimes against him; knowing Yu Zhun and Yan had long borne a grudge, he recommended Yu as military commissioner of Jingnan to spy on Yan's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan wanted to frame him on false charges, so he appointed Yu Zhun—who had long been at odds with Liu Yan—as military commissioner of Jingnan to watch Yan's every move.

sentences.zh: 準乃奏晏與硃泚書祈救解，言多怨望，炎又證成其事，上以為然。

translations.literal: Yu Zhun then memorialized that Yan had written to Zhu Ci begging rescue and release, his words full of resentment; Yang Yan further corroborated the matter, and the emperor considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun reported that Yan had written to the rebel Zhu Ci pleading for rescue, his language seething with grievance; Yang Yan bolstered the accusation, and the emperor believed it.

sentences.zh: 是月庚午，晏已受誅，使回奏報，誣晏以忠州謀叛，下詔暴言其罪，時年六十六，天下冤之。

translations.literal: That month on the gengwu day, Yan had already been executed; the envoy returned to report, slandering Yan as plotting rebellion at Zhongzhou; an edict was issued proclaiming his crimes. He was then sixty-six; all under heaven deemed it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of that month Yan had already been put to death. When the envoy returned, he falsely claimed Yan had plotted rebellion from his exile in Zhongzhou; the court issued an edict publicly listing his alleged crimes. Yan was sixty-six years old, and people everywhere regarded his execution as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 家屬徙嶺表，連累者數十人。

translations.literal: His household was relocated beyond the Ling passes; several tens were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: His family was banished to the far south beyond the mountain passes, and dozens of others were dragged down with them.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，上悟，方錄晏子執經，授太常博士；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, when the emperor came to understand, he only then recorded Yan's son Zhijing and appointed him as director in the Imperial Academy;
translations.idiomatic: In 789, once the emperor realized his error, he recalled Yan's son Zhijing and appointed him director of learning at the Imperial Academy;

sentences.zh: 少子宗經，秘書郎。

translations.literal: His younger son Zongjing became a secretary in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son, Zongjing, was appointed secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 執經上請削官贈父，特追贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhijing memorialized asking to relinquish his rank to posthumously honor his father; a special posthumous appointment as prefect of Zhengzhou was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing petitioned to surrender his own office so his father might be honored posthumously; the throne made a special grant and posthumously enfeoffed Liu Yan as prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 第五琦，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Di Wuqi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Di Wuqi hailed from Chang'an in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事兄華，敬順過人。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he served his elder brother Hua with deference surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents young and waited on his elder brother Hua with a devotion few could match.

sentences.zh: 及長，有吏才，以富國強兵之術自任。

translations.literal: When grown, he had talent for administration and took upon himself methods to enrich the state and strengthen the army.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he showed real administrative talent and devoted himself to schemes for filling the treasury and building military strength.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，事韋堅，堅敗貶官。

translations.literal: Early in the Tianbao era he served Wei Jian; when Wei fell, he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao years he entered the service of Wei Jian, and when Wei was ruined and disgraced, Di Wuqi was demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 累至須江丞，時太守賀蘭進明甚重之。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to assistant magistrate of Xujiang; at the time the prefect Helan Jinming greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to assistant magistrate of Xujiang, where Prefect Helan Jinming held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 會安祿山反，進明遷北海郡太守，奏琦為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Jinming was transferred to be prefect of Beihai Commandery and recommended Qi as recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Jinming was reassigned as prefect of Beihai Commandery and had Di Wuqi appointed his chief administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 祿山已陷河間、信都等五郡，進明未有戰功，玄宗大怒，遣中使封刀促之，曰：「收地不得，即斬進明之首。」

translations.literal: Lushan had already taken five commanderies including Hejian and Xindu; Jinming had achieved no military merit. Emperor Xuanzong was greatly angered and sent a palace envoy bearing a sword to urge him, saying: "If you do not recover the territory, then Jinming's head will be cut off at once.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan had already overrun five commanderies, including Hejian and Xindu, yet Jinming had won no victories on the field. Furious, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched a eunuch bearing an imperial sword with this ultimatum: "Recover the lost territory, or Helan Jinming loses his head.

sentences.zh: 進明惶懼，莫知所出，琦乃勸令厚以財帛募勇敢士，出奇力戰，遂收所陷之郡。

translations.literal: Jinming was fearful and knew not what to do; Qi then counseled him to lavish wealth and silks to recruit daring men, to strike with surprise and fight fiercely, and thereby recovered the lost commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming panicked and saw no way out. Di Wuqi advised him to pour gold and goods into recruiting bold fighters, take the enemy by surprise, and fight with all force—and in this way they retook the fallen commanderies.

sentences.zh: 令琦奏事，至蜀中，琦得謁見，奏言：「方今之急在兵，兵之強弱在賦，賦之所出，江淮居多。

translations.literal: He had Qi report to court; reaching Shu, Qi obtained an audience and memorialized: "The present urgency lies in armies; armies' strength or weakness lies in taxation; of tax sources, the Jiang-Huai region supplies most.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming sent Di Wuqi to report to the throne. On reaching the Shu region, Qi gained an audience and argued: "Our most pressing need is military strength, military strength depends on revenue, and most of that revenue comes from the Jiang-Huai basin.

sentences.zh: 若假臣職任，使濟軍須，臣能使賞給之資，不勞聖慮。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty grants me authority and commission so I may supply the army's needs, I can provide funds for rewards and disbursements without troubling the sage mind.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will grant me the authority to meet the army's needs, I can find the money for pay and supplies without burdening the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大喜，即日拜監察御史，勾當江淮租庸使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased; that very day Qi was appointed investigating censor and put in charge of Jiang-Huai land-and-labor tax commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and the same day named Qi investigating censor and commissioner for Jiang-Huai tax collection.

sentences.zh: 尋拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed attendant censor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to attendant censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋加山南等五道度支使，促辦應卒，事無違闕。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made commissioner of disbursements for five circuits including Shannan; he pressed urgent completion and nothing fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given charge of fiscal affairs for five circuits, including Shannan, and drove every urgent task to completion without a single lapse.

sentences.zh: 遷司金郎中、兼御史中丞，使如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the Bureau of Coinage, concurrently vice censor-in-chief; his commissioner posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Bureau of Coinage and vice censor-in-chief while keeping his existing commissioner duties.

sentences.zh: 於是創立鹽法，就山海井竈收榷其鹽，官置吏出糶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established salt law: at mountains, seas, wells, and salterns salt was levied and monopolized; the government appointed officials to sell it forth.
translations.idiomatic: He then created the salt monopoly: the state took control of salt production at coastal salterns, inland wells, and mountain sources, and sold the salt through official agents.

sentences.zh: 其舊業戶並浮人願為業者，免其雜徭，隸鹽鐵使，盜煮私市罪有差。

translations.literal: Former salt-producing households and floating persons wishing to enter the trade were exempted from miscellaneous corvée, subordinated to the salt-and-iron commissioner; penalties for illicit boiling and private sale were graded.
translations.idiomatic: Established producers and newcomers who wished to join the trade were freed from miscellaneous labor obligations and placed under the salt commission; theft of the salt trade through private boiling or sale carried graded punishments.

sentences.zh: 百姓除租庸外，無得橫賦，人不益稅而上用以饒。

translations.literal: The common people beyond rent-and-corvée had no arbitrary levies added; people were not increased in tax yet state use became abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary taxpayers faced no new levies beyond the regular land-and-labor dues, yet the treasury grew flush without raising the tax burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎、兼御史丞，專判度支，領河南等道支度都勾當轉運租庸鹽鐵鑄錢、司農太府出納、山南東西江西淮南館驛等使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of revenue, concurrently vice censor, with sole judgment of disbursements, heading commissioners for Henan and other circuits' supply, transport, rent-and-corvée, salt-and-iron, coin casting, grain and treasury intake and outflow, Shannan east and west, Jiangxi, Huainan postal stations, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of revenue and vice censor-in-chief, he took sole charge of national finance and simultaneously headed a sprawling portfolio: supply and transport for Henan and other regions, tax collection, the salt monopoly, coinage, grain and treasury operations, and postal services from Shannan to Jiangxi and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，以本官加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan, on his existing office was added the designation of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he received the grand councilor title while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 初，琦以國用未足，幣重貨輕，乃請鑄乾元重寶錢，以一當十行用之。

translations.literal: At first, because state use was insufficient and coin was heavy while goods were light, Qi requested casting Qianyuan Heavy Treasure coin, using one as ten in circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, finding the treasury short and goods dear while copper coin remained scarce, Qi proposed minting the Qianyuan Heavy Treasure coin, valued at ten ordinary coins each.

sentences.zh: 及作相，又請更鑄重輪乾元錢，一當五十，與乾元錢及開元通寶錢三品並行。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, he again requested recasting heavy-rim Qianyuan coin, one counting as fifty, circulating alongside Qianyuan coin and Kaiyuan tongbao in three denominations.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated to chancellor, he pushed for another coin—the heavy-rim Qianyuan piece, worth fifty—and let all three denominations circulate side by side with the standard Kaiyuan coin.

sentences.zh: 既而谷價騰貴，餓殣死亡，枕藉道路，又盜鑄爭起，中外皆以琦變法之弊，封奏日聞。

translations.literal: Before long grain prices soared; starved corpses died, strewn along the roads; moreover counterfeiting disputes arose; within and without all attributed it to Qi's monetary reform's harms, memorials arriving daily.
translations.idiomatic: Soon grain prices skyrocketed, famine corpses piled along the highways, counterfeiters swarmed, and from every quarter came daily memorials blaming Di Wuqi's currency experiments for the disaster.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年十月，貶忠州長史，既在道，有告琦受人黃金二百兩者，遣御史劉期光追按之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Qianyuan second year, he was demoted to chief administrator of Zhongzhou; already on the road, someone reported Qi had received two hundred taels of gold; censor Liu Qiguang was sent to pursue and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 759 he was demoted to chief administrator of Zhongzhou. While still en route, an informer accused him of accepting two hundred taels of gold, and Censor Liu Qiguang was dispatched to pursue the case.

sentences.zh: 琦對曰：二百兩金十三斤重，忝為宰相，不可自持。

translations.literal: Qi replied: "Two hundred taels of gold weighs thirteen jin; I am shamed to have been chancellor—this cannot be carried personally.
translations.idiomatic: Qi answered: "Two hundred taels is thirteen jin of gold—too much for a man who once sat in the chancellery to haul about on his own person.

sentences.zh: 若其付受有憑，即請準法科罪。」

translations.literal: If there is evidence of receipt and delivery, then I ask punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: If there is proof I took it, apply the statute and punish me accordingly.

sentences.zh: 期光以為此是琦伏罪也，遽奏之，請除名，配流夷州，馳驛發遣，仍差綱領送至彼。

translations.literal: Qiguang regarded this as Qi's confession of guilt; he hastily memorialized, requesting removal from registers, assignment to exile in Yizhou, dispatch by express relay, and still appointing escort leaders to deliver him there.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiguang took this for a confession. He rushed a memorial asking that Qi be struck from the rolls, exiled to Yizhou, and hustled there by express courier under armed escort.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，起為朗州刺史，甚有能政，入遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: Early in Baoying, he was recalled as prefect of Langzhou; his capable governance was notable; he entered and was promoted to adviser to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Baoying era he was recalled to serve as prefect of Langzhou, where he governed ably; later he returned to court as adviser to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 屬吐蕃寇陷京師，代宗幸陜，關內副元帥郭子儀請琦為糧料使、兼御史大夫，充關內元帥副使。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided and seized the capital, Emperor Daizong fled to Shaan; deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei Guo Ziyi requested Qi as grain supply commissioner and concurrent censor-in-chief, serving as deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetan forces stormed the capital and Emperor Daizong withdrew to Shaan, Guo Ziyi—the deputy commander of Guannei—asked that Di Wuqi serve as grain commissioner and censor-in-chief, and as his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as metropolitan prefect of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 車駕克復，專判度支，兼諸道鑄錢鹽鐵轉運常平等使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage recovered the capital, he solely judged disbursements, concurrently heading commissioners for all circuits' coin casting, salt-and-iron, transport, and grain price stabilization.
translations.idiomatic: After the court returned to the capital, he again took exclusive charge of national finance and simultaneously oversaw coinage, the salt monopoly, transport, and grain price stabilization across the provinces.

sentences.zh: 累封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually ennobled as Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 又加京兆尹，改戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: Again added as metropolitan prefect; changed to vice minister of revenue, judging disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: He later resumed the post of metropolitan prefect while also serving as vice minister of revenue with control of national finances.

sentences.zh: 前後領財賦十余年。

translations.literal: In all he led finance and taxation for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than a decade he directed the empire's fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩伏誅，琦坐與款狎，出為處州刺史，歷饒、湖二州。

translations.literal: When Yu Chao'en was executed for his crimes, Qi was implicated for intimacy with him; he was sent out as prefect of Chuzhou, then served Rao and Hu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the eunuch Yu Chao'en was executed, Di Wuqi was punished for his close ties to him and banished first to Chuzhou, then to Rao and Hu.

sentences.zh: 入為太子賓客、東都留司。

translations.literal: He entered as adviser to the heir apparent and as a nominal official retained in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to court as adviser to the crown prince and held a nominal post in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 上以其材，將復任用，召還京師，信宿而卒，年七十，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: The emperor for his talent was about to employ him again; he was recalled to the capital; after two nights he died, age seventy; posthumously granted lesser tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed by his ability, was preparing to bring him back into service and summoned him to the capital—but within two nights Di Wuqi was dead, aged seventy. He was posthumously honored as Lesser Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 子峰，峰婦鄭氏女，皆以孝著，旌表其門。

translations.literal: His son Feng—Feng's wife, a daughter of the Zheng clan—both were noted for filial piety; their gate was honored with an inscribed commendation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng and Feng's wife, a daughter of the Zheng family, were both famed for filial devotion; the throne had their household gate publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 班宏，衛州汲人也。

translations.literal: Ban Hong was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong came from Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖思簡，春官員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Si Jian was auxiliary director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Si Jian had served as auxiliary director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父景倩，秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Jing Qian was director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing Qian had been director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 宏少舉進士，授右司禦胄曹，後為薛景先鳳翔掌書記，又為高適劍南觀察判官，累拜大理司直，攝監察御史。

translations.literal: Hong in youth passed the jinshi examination, was appointed armoury clerk in the Right Guard, later served Xue Jingxian as recorder in Fengxiang, then Gao Shi's judicial aide in Jiannan observation, rose to investigating judge in the Court of Judicial Review, acting investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong passed the jinshi examination in his youth and began as an armoury clerk in the Right Guard. He later served as staff secretary for Xue Jingxian in Fengxiang and as judicial aide to Gao Shi in Jiannan, eventually rising to investigating judge in the Court of Judicial Review while acting as an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時青城山有妖賊張安居以左道惑眾，事覺，多誣引大將，冀以緩死，宏驗理而速殺之，人心乃安。

translations.literal: At the time on Mount Qingcheng the demonic bandit Zhang Anju used heterodox ways to delude the masses; when exposed, he falsely implicated many generals hoping to delay death; Hong verified the case and swiftly executed him; people's hearts were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the sorcerer-rebel Zhang Anju on Mount Qingcheng was caught using forbidden rites to gather followers, he tried to save his life by falsely naming high generals as accomplices. Ban Hong investigated, swiftly condemned him, and restored public confidence.

sentences.zh: 既而郭英乂代適，以厭人望，奏署秘書郎，兼雒令，以疾免。

translations.literal: Before long Guo Yingyi replaced Shi; to sate public expectation, he memorialized appointing Hong secretary and concurrently magistrate of Luo; he was dismissed for illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Yingyi succeeded Gao Shi, he placated public opinion by appointing Ban Hong secretary and magistrate of Luoyang, though illness soon forced Hong to leave office.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，遷起居舍人，尋兼理匭使，四遷至給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali he was transferred to diarist-attendant; soon concurrently complaint-box commissioner; through four promotions to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 768 he was made imperial diarist, soon added oversight of the imperial complaint box, and after four promotions reached the rank of supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 時李寶臣卒於其位，子惟嶽匿喪求位，上遣宏使成德問疾，且喻之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Baochen died in office; his son Wei Yue concealed the funeral seeking succession; the emperor sent Hong as envoy to Chengde to inquire after illness and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: When regional strongman Li Baochen died in office, his son Wei Yue hid the death to seize power. The emperor dispatched Ban Hong to Chengde under the pretense of a condolence visit to warn him against it.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽厚賂宏，皆不受，還報合旨，遷刑部侍郎，兼京官考使。

translations.literal: Wei Yue lavishly bribed Hong; he accepted none; on return his report accorded with intent; he was promoted vice minister of justice, concurrently metropolitan official examiner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue tried to buy him off with lavish bribes, but Hong refused every gift. His report pleased the throne, and he was promoted to vice minister of justice with charge of metropolitan official evaluations.

sentences.zh: 時右僕射崔寧考兵部侍郎劉乃上下，宏駁曰：「夷荒靖難，專在節制，尺籍伍符，不校省司。

translations.literal: At the time right vice director Cui Ning rated vice minister of war Liu Nai as average; Hong rebutted: "Pacifying barbarians and wild lands, the specialty lies in military commissioners; roster tallies and unit tallies are not checked by central departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director Cui Ning rated Liu Nai, vice minister of war, as merely average, Ban Hong objected: "Frontier pacification rests with the military commissioners; central ministries do not audit their muster rolls and unit rosters.

sentences.zh: 夫上行宣美之名，則下開趨競之路；

translations.literal: When superiors give names of proclaimed merit, then inferiors open paths of striving competition;
translations.idiomatic: When superiors hand out hollow praise, subordinates learn to scramble for favor;

sentences.zh: 上行阿容，下必朋黨。」

translations.literal: When superiors practice flattery and tolerance, inferiors must form factions.
translations.idiomatic: when superiors indulge flattery, those below will inevitably form factions.

sentences.zh: 因削去之。

translations.literal: Therefore he struck it out.
translations.idiomatic: He deleted the inflated rating.

sentences.zh: 乃知而謝曰：「乃雖不敏，敢掠一美以僥二罪乎？」

translations.literal: Nai, knowing this, apologized: "Though Nai is not keen, dare I seize one merit to gamble for two crimes?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Nai understood and apologized: "I may lack wit, but would I grab unearned credit and risk double blame?

sentences.zh: 尋除吏部侍郎，為汪蕃會盟使李揆之副。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of personnel, deputy to Li Kui, envoy for alliance with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made vice minister of personnel and deputy to Li Kui, envoy to the Tibetan alliance talks.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，仍歲旱蝗，上以賦調為急，改戶部侍郎，為度支使韓滉之副。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan, drought and locusts continued years; the emperor made tax collection urgent; Hong was changed to vice minister of revenue as deputy to disbursement commissioner Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenyuan era, drought and locusts struck year after year and tax collection became the emperor's top priority; Ban Hong was made vice minister of revenue and deputy to fiscal chief Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，復副竇參。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director; again served as deputy to Dou Can.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director and again served as deputy—this time to Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 參初為大理司直，宏已為刑部侍郎，及參為相，領度支，上以宏久司國計，因令副之。

translations.literal: Can at first was investigating judge in Judicial Review; Hong was already vice minister of justice; when Can became chancellor and headed disbursements, the emperor because Hong long managed state accounts had him serve as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can had been a mere judge, Ban Hong was already vice minister of justice; once Can rose to chancellor and took charge of finance, the emperor paired him with Hong, who had managed the national ledgers for years.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「朕藉參宰相以臨遠，眾務悉委於卿，勿以辭也。」

translations.literal: And said: "I rely on Chancellor Can to oversee distant matters; all affairs I entirely entrust to you—do not decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "I need Chancellor Dou to manage affairs far afield; I am placing every detail of finance in your hands—do not refuse.

sentences.zh: 參以先貴，常私解悅之曰：「參後來，一朝居尚書之上，甚不自安，一年之後，當歸此使。」

translations.literal: Can because Hong had been senior, often privately placated him saying: "Can came later; for one morning to sit above director—I am very ill at ease; after one year I will return this commission to you.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hong outranked him in seniority, Dou Can often privately reassured him: "I arrived late and feel uneasy sitting above you as director; in a year I will give this commission back to you.

sentences.zh: 宏心喜，歲餘，參絕不復言。

translations.literal: Hong's heart rejoiced; after a year and more, Can never spoke of it again.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong believed him—but more than a year passed and Can never mentioned it again.

sentences.zh: 宏性剛愎，為人間之，且怒食言，公事多異。

translations.literal: Hong's nature was stubborn; someone told him of this; he also resented the broken promise; public affairs often diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn by nature, Ban Hong learned of the broken promise, seethed at Dou Can's treachery, and their official dealings turned contentious.

sentences.zh: 揚子院，鹽鐵轉運委藏也，宏以御史中丞徐粲主之，既不理，且以賄聞，參欲代之，宏執不可。

translations.literal: Yangzi depot was the entrusted storehouse for salt-and-iron transport; Hong had vice censor Xu Can manage it—he neither administered well, and bribery was reported; Can wished to replace him; Hong obstinately refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzhou depot held salt-and-iron transport reserves under Vice Censor Xu Can, who neglected the job and was rumored to be taking bribes. Dou Can wanted to replace him, but Ban Hong dug in his heels and refused.

sentences.zh: 參又選諸院吏，未嘗訪宏，乃疏參所用者過惡以聞，事輒留中。

translations.literal: Can again selected depot clerks without ever consulting Hong; Hong then memorialized the faults of those Can employed; matters were repeatedly held in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can began appointing depot staff without consulting Hong, so Hong sent up memorials detailing the misconduct of Can's choices—and the emperor kept those reports under wraps.

sentences.zh: 無何，參以使勞加吏部尚書，而宏進封蕭國公，怨參以虛號寵之，間惡愈甚。

translations.literal: Before long Can for mission merit was promoted to minister of personnel; Hong advanced to Duke of Xiao; he resented Can for honoring him with an empty title; mutual detestation grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dou Can was promoted to minister of personnel for his service on missions, while Ban Hong was ennobled as Duke of Xiao. Hong saw the title as empty flattery and their mutual hostility deepened.

sentences.zh: 每奉詔營建，宏必極壯麗，親程課役，又厚結權幸以傾參。

translations.literal: Whenever ordered to undertake construction, Hong always made it maximally grand, personally measured work obligations; also he lavishly bonded with powerful favorites to topple Can.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tasked with imperial construction projects, Ban Hong built on the grandest scale and supervised labor personally, while cultivating powerful favorites at court to undermine Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 張滂先善於宏，宏薦為司農少卿，及參欲以滂分掌江淮鹽鐵，詢之於宏，宏以滂嫉惡，慮以法繩徐粲，因曰：「滂強戾難制，不可用。」

translations.literal: Zhang Pang had first been on good terms with Hong; Hong recommended him as vice director of agriculture; when Can wished Pang to share management of Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron, he consulted Hong; Hong because Pang was jealous and harsh, fearing he would use law to bind Xu Can, therefore said: "Pang is violent and obstinate, hard to control—not usable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang had once been Ban Hong's ally, and Hong had helped make him vice director of agriculture. When Dou Can proposed splitting Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron duties with Pang, he asked Hong's view. Hong knew Pang was fierce and incorruptible and feared he would prosecute Xu Can, so he said, "Pang is harsh and unmanageable—he cannot be used.

sentences.zh: 滂知之。

translations.literal: Pang knew of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang learned of the slight.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，參遂為上所疏，乃讓度支使，遂以宏專判，而參不欲使務悉歸於宏，問計京兆尹薛玨，玨曰：「二子交惡，而滂剛決，若分鹽鐵轉運於滂，必能制宏。」

translations.literal: Third month of year eight, Can was therefore denounced to the emperor; he yielded the disbursement commission; Hong was then given sole judgment; yet Can did not wish all affairs to fall wholly to Hong; he consulted Metropolitan Prefect Xue Jue; Jue said: "The two men are mutually hostile, and Pang is firm and decisive; if salt-and-iron transport is divided to Pang, he will surely be able to restrain Hong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 792 Dou Can fell from imperial favor and surrendered the finance commission to Ban Hong—but Can did not want Hong controlling everything. He consulted Metropolitan Prefect Xue Jue, who advised: "Those two are enemies, and Pang is tough and resolute; give him salt-and-iron transport and he can check Hong.

sentences.zh: 參乃薦滂為戶部侍郎、鹽鐵使、判轉運，尚隸於宏以悅之。

translations.literal: Can then recommended Pang as vice minister of revenue, salt-and-iron commissioner, judging transport, still subordinate to Hong to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can accordingly recommended Zhang Pang as vice minister of revenue, salt commissioner, and transport supervisor—formally under Hong, to keep him appeased.

sentences.zh: 江淮兩稅，悉宏主之，置巡院，然令宏、滂共擇其官。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai double tax was entirely managed by Hong; inspection depots were established; yet Hong and Pang together were to select their officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong kept control of the Jiang-Huai land tax and set up inspection offices, but both men were told to jointly appoint their staff.

sentences.zh: 滂請鹽鐵舊簿書於宏，宏不與之。

translations.literal: Pang requested old salt-and-iron ledgers from Hong; Hong would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang asked Ban Hong for the old salt-and-iron account books; Hong refused to hand them over.

sentences.zh: 每署院官，宏、滂更相是非，莫有用者。

translations.literal: Each time depot officials were appointed, Hong and Pang alternately negated each other; none could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Every time one of them nominated a depot official, the other vetoed the choice, and positions stayed empty.

sentences.zh: 滂乃奏曰：「班宏與臣相戾，巡院多闕官。

translations.literal: Pang then memorialized: "Ban Hong is at odds with me; inspection depots have many vacant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang memorialized: "Ban Hong and I are at loggerheads, and many inspection posts stand unfilled.

sentences.zh: 臣掌財賦，國家大計，職不修，無所逃罪。

translations.literal: I manage finance and taxation—the great plan of the state; if duties are not maintained, there is no escaping guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I oversee revenue—the lifeblood of the state. If I fail in my duties, I cannot escape blame.

sentences.zh: 今宏若此，何以輯事？」

translations.literal: Now if Hong is like this, how can affairs be assembled?
translations.idiomatic: With Hong acting like this, how can the work get done?

sentences.zh: 遂令分掌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an order was issued to divide management.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to split the duties between them.

sentences.zh: 無幾，宏言於宰相趙憬、陸贄曰：「宏職轉運，年運江淮米五十萬斛，前年增七十萬斛，以實太倉，幸無過。

translations.literal: Before long Hong spoke to chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: "Hong's duty is transport—each year fifty thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice shipped; the year before last increased to seven hundred thousand shi to fill the Great Storehouse; fortunately without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ban Hong told Chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: "In my transport duties I once moved five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai grain each year, and two years ago seven hundred thousand shi to fill the Great Storehouse—and I met every target.

sentences.zh: 今職移於人，不知何謂？」

translations.literal: Now duties shifted to another—what is this to mean?
translations.idiomatic: Now my duties have been handed to someone else—what am I to make of that?

sentences.zh: 滂時在側，忿然曰：「尚書失言甚矣！

translations.literal: Pang was then at the side; angrily he said: "Director, you misspeak greatly!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang, who was present, snapped: "Director, you go too far!

sentences.zh: 若運務畢舉，朝廷固不奪之，蓋由喪公錢、縱奸吏故也。

translations.literal: If transport duties were fully accomplished, the court naturally would not strip them; it is because of losing public money and indulging corrupt clerks.
translations.idiomatic: If you had truly done your job, the court would never have taken transport away from you. You lost it because you squandered public funds and protected crooked subordinates.

sentences.zh: 且凡為度支胥吏，不一歲，資累鉅萬，僮馬第宅，僭於王公，非盜官財何以致是？

translations.literal: Moreover all who are disbursement clerks, within one year assets accumulate in the tens of thousands; slaves, horses, mansions surpassing kings and dukes—if not stealing official wealth, how attain this?
translations.idiomatic: And every clerk in the finance office amasses fortunes of tens of thousands within a year—slaves, horses, mansions fit for princes. How else could they afford it except by robbing the treasury?

sentences.zh: 道呼喧喧，無不知之，聖上故令滂分掌。

translations.literal: Along the roads the clamor is loud—none do not know; the sage emperor therefore had Pang divide management.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone on the road knows it, which is exactly why His Majesty ordered me to share the duties.

sentences.zh: 公向所言，無乃歸怨於上乎、」宏默然不對。

translations.literal: What the lord just said—might it not shift blame onto the sovereign?" Hong silently did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Are you not pinning the blame on the emperor himself?" Ban Hong fell silent.

sentences.zh: 是日，宏稱疾於第，滂往問之，宏不見，憬、贄乃以宏、滂之言上聞。

translations.literal: That day Hong claimed illness at his residence; Pang went to inquire; Hong would not see him; Jing and Zhi then reported Hong and Pang's words to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That day Ban Hong feigned illness at home. When Zhang Pang came to visit, Hong refused to see him. Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi reported both men's words to the throne.

sentences.zh: 由是遵大歷故事，如劉晏、韓滉所分。

translations.literal: Thereby following Dali precedent, as Liu Yan and Han Huang had divided duties.
translations.idiomatic: The court then reverted to the Dali-era arrangement, dividing finance as Liu Yan and Han Huang once had.

sentences.zh: 滂至揚州按徐粲，逮仆妾子侄，得贓鉅萬，乃徙嶺表。

translations.literal: Pang reached Yangzhou to investigate Xu Can; arrested maids, concubines, sons and nephews; obtained bribes in the tens of thousands; then Xu was exiled beyond the Ling passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang went to Yangzhou to prosecute Xu Can, seized his household and kin, uncovered bribes totaling tens of thousands, and had him banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 故參得罪，宏頗有力焉。

translations.literal: Thus when Can incurred guilt, Hong contributed considerable force to it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can finally fell, Ban Hong had played no small part in bringing him down.

sentences.zh: 勤恪官署，晨入夕歸，下吏勞而未嘗厭苦，清白勤幹，稱之於時。

translations.literal: Diligent at office, entering at dawn and returning at evening; subordinates labored yet he never showed weariness; pure, white, diligent, capable—praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He was tireless at his desk, arriving at dawn and leaving at dusk; though his staff toiled endlessly he never complained. His honesty and industry won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年七月卒，年七十三，廢朝，加贈，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: Seventh month Zhenyuan eighth year he died, age seventy-three; court mourning suspended; additional posthumous honors; posthumous title Jing (Reverent).
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of 792, aged seventy-three. Court audiences were suspended, extra honors granted, and he was posthumously titled "Reverent."

sentences.zh: 王紹，本家於太原，今為京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wang Shao's ancestral home was in Taiyuan; now he was a person of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao's family originally came from Taiyuan but now lived in Wannian, in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 舊名與憲宗同，永貞年改焉。

translations.literal: His old given name was the same as Emperor Xianzong's; in the Yongzhen era it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name matched that of the future Emperor Xianzong, so it was changed during the Yongzhen era.

sentences.zh: 少時，顏真卿器重之，因紹舊名，字之曰德素，奏授武康尉。

translations.literal: In youth Yan Zhenqing greatly valued him; because of Shao's old name, he gave him the courtesy name Desu, memorialized appointing him assistant magistrate of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yan Zhenqing took a liking to him, gave him the courtesy name Desu because of his former name, and had him appointed assistant magistrate of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 蕭復為常州刺史，辟為從事；

translations.literal: When Xiao Fu was prefect of Changzhou, he recruited him as staff member;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Fu served as prefect of Changzhou, he recruited Wang Shao as a staff officer;

sentences.zh: 包佶領租庸鹽鐵，亦以紹為判官。

translations.literal: Bao Ji headed rent-and-corvée and salt-and-iron; he also took Shao as judicial aide.
translations.idiomatic: and when Bao Ji took charge of tax and salt affairs, he too made Shao his aide.

sentences.zh: 時李希烈阻兵，江淮租輸，所在艱阻，特移運路自潁入汴。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xilie blocked with troops; Jiang-Huai rent-and-transport revenue, everywhere was difficult and obstructed; the transport route was specially diverted from Ying into Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xilie was using military force to obstruct communications, making it difficult to move Jiang-Huai rent and transport revenue through many areas, so the transport route was specially redirected from Ying into Bian.

sentences.zh: 紹奉佶表詣闕，屬德宗西幸，紹乃督緣路輕貨，趣金、商路，倍程出洋州以赴行在。

translations.literal: Shao carried Ji's memorial to the capital; just when Dezong was traveling west, Shao then superintended light goods along the route, took the Jin and Shang route, doubling pace to exit through Yang Prefecture to reach the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao bore Bao Ji's memorial to the capital. When Emperor Dezong was forced west, Shao took charge of light goods along the route, hastened via the Jin and Shang roadways, and at double speed crossed through Yang Prefecture to reach the imperial party.

sentences.zh: 德宗親勞之，謂紹曰：「六軍未有春服，我猶衣裘。」

translations.literal: Dezong personally comforted him, saying to Shao: "The Six Armies have no spring garments; I still wear furs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong received him in person and said to Wang Shao, "The armies have no spring clothing, and I still wear furs.

sentences.zh: 紹俯伏流涕，奏曰：「包佶令臣間道進奉數約五十萬。」

translations.literal: Shao prostrated himself weeping and memorialized: "Bao Ji ordered me by a bypath to present tribute of about five hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao prostrated himself in tears and reported, "Bao Ji has directed me by a secret route to deliver tribute of roughly five hundred thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 上曰：道路回遠，經費懸急，卿之所奏，豈可望耶？」
