translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The roads are circuitous and distant, expenses are urgently needed; what you memorialized—how can that be hoped for?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The roads are long and difficult, and funds are desperately needed. What you report—can we really expect it?"

sentences.zh: 後五日而所督繼至，上深賴焉。

translations.literal: Five days later what he superintended arrived in succession; the Emperor deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the goods he had overseen began arriving, and the emperor relied deeply on him.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，為倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he was Assistant Director in the Bureau of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he served as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 時屬兵革旱蝗之後，令戶部收闕官俸，兼稅茶及諸色無名之錢，以為水旱之備。

translations.literal: The time fell after warfare, drought, and locusts; the Bureau of Revenue was ordered to collect vacant official salaries, and additionally tax tea and various unnamed miscellaneous taxes, as preparation against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: This came in the aftermath of war, drought, and locust plagues. The Bureau of Revenue was ordered to collect unclaimed salaries, levy a tea tax, and impose various miscellaneous unnamed levies as reserves against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 紹自拜倉部，便準詔主判，及遷戶部、兵部郎中，皆獨司其務。

translations.literal: From the time Shao received the Granary post, he immediately per edict chiefly presided; when transferred to Director in the Revenue and Military bureaus, in each case he alone managed the duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Wang Shao took the Granary post, he was immediately put in charge by imperial order. When he was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Revenue and then the Bureau of Military Affairs, he alone handled the work in each case.

sentences.zh: 擢拜戶部侍郎，尋判度支。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and soon presided over disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and shortly thereafter put in charge of the finance office.

sentences.zh: 後二年，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Two years later he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗臨馭歲久，機務不由臺司，自竇參、陸贄已後，宰臣備位而已。

translations.literal: Dezong had held the throne long; key affairs did not pass through the Secretariat; from Dou Can and Lu Zhi onward, chancellors merely filled positions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had ruled for many years, and important business no longer ran through the Secretariat. After Dou Can and Lu Zhi, chancellors were little more than figureheads.

sentences.zh: 德宗以紹謹密，恩遇特異，凡主重務八年，政之大小，多所訪決。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Shao was careful and discreet, gave him exceptionally special favor; for eight years he managed heavy duties, and on affairs great and small the Emperor often consulted him for decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong valued Wang Shao for his caution and discretion and showered him with exceptional favor. He held major responsibilities for eight years, and on matters large and small the emperor frequently sought his judgment.

sentences.zh: 紹未賞泄漏，亦不矜衒。

translations.literal: Shao never once leaked, nor did he boast and show off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao never leaked a confidence, nor did he flaunt his influence.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，王叔文始奪其權，拜兵部尚書，尋除檢校吏部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, Wang Shuwen first stripped him of power; he was appointed Minister of Military Affairs, and soon made Acting Minister of Personnel and Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Wang Shuwen stripped him of real authority. He was appointed Minister of Military Affairs, then shortly relieved as Acting Minister of Personnel and left in charge as Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷檢校尚書右僕射、徐州刺史、武寧軍節度，復以濠、泗二州隸焉。

translations.literal: In early Yuanhe he was transferred to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prefect of Xuzhou, and Military Governor of Wu'ning Circuit; Haozhou and Sizhou were again placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhe era he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, prefect of Xuzhou, and military governor of Wu'ning Circuit, with Haozhou and Sizhou again placed under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 時承張愔之後，兵驕難治，紹修輯軍政，人甚安之。

translations.literal: At the time succeeding after Zhang Yin, the troops were arrogant and hard to govern; Shao repaired and ordered military administration, and the people were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Zhang Yin when the soldiery had grown arrogant and unruly. Wang Shao restored military discipline, and the people found peace.

sentences.zh: 六年，征拜兵部尚書，兼判戶部事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Military Affairs, concurrently presiding over Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was recalled to serve as Minister of Military Affairs and given concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，年七十二，贈左僕射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, age seventy-two; posthumously made Left Vice Director; posthumous title Jing (Reverent).
translations.idiomatic: He died in 814, aged seventy-two. He was posthumously made Left Vice Director and given the posthumous title "Reverent."

sentences.zh: 李巽，字令叔，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Xun, courtesy name Ling Shu, was a native of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, courtesy name Ling Shu, came from Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少苦心為學，以明經調補華州參軍，拔萃登科，授鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: In youth he painstakingly studied; through the classics examination he was appointed Huazhou aide; selected in the superior examination and passed; granted Assistant Magistrate of E County.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he applied himself rigorously to learning. He passed the classics examination and was appointed aide in Huazhou. After winning selection in the superior examination he was made assistant magistrate of E County.

sentences.zh: 周歷臺省，由左司郎中出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through the Secretariat and Chancellery offices; from Director in the Left Bureau he went out as Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in various posts in the Secretariat and Chancellery, and left the capital from his post as Director in the Left Bureau to become prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召為給事中，出為湖南觀察使，銳於為理。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned as Supervising Censor, sent out as Hunan Observation Commissioner; he was keen on governance.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to serve as a Supervising Secretariat Drafter, then sent out as commissioner of Hunan, where he governed with sharp efficiency.

sentences.zh: 五年，改江西觀察使，加檢校散騎常侍、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, with additional Acting Regular Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In his fifth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as observation commissioner, with the additional titles of Acting Regular Palace Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 巽持下以法，吏不敢欺，而動必察之。

translations.literal: Xun held subordinates by law; clerks did not dare deceive, yet every movement he surely investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun governed his subordinates strictly by law. Clerks did not dare cheat him—and he scrutinized every move they made.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Li Xun was brought back to serve as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 司徒杜佑判度支鹽鐵轉運使，以巽幹治，奏為副使。

translations.literal: Duke Du You presided over finance, salt, iron, and transport; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Du You headed the finance, salt, iron, and transport commission. Impressed by Li Xun's administrative skill, he recommended him as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 佑辭重位，巽遂專領度支鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: You declined the heavy post; Xun then solely headed the Finance and Salt Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Du You stepped down from the heavy office, Li Xun took sole charge of the finance and salt commission.

sentences.zh: 榷筦之法，號為難重，唯大歷中僕射劉晏雅得其術，賦入豐羨。

translations.literal: The monopoly-and-control laws were called difficult and heavy; only in the Dali era Vice Director Liu Yan elegantly mastered their technique, and tax revenue was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The state monopoly system was notoriously difficult to manage. Only in the Dali era had Vice Director Liu Yan truly mastered it, yielding abundant revenue.

sentences.zh: 巽掌使一年，征課所入，類晏之多歲，明年過之，又一年加一百八十萬貫。

translations.literal: Xun held the commission one year; revenue collected matched Yan's many plentiful years; the next year surpassed it; in another year he added one million eight hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year in office Li Xun's tax collections matched Liu Yan's best years. The next year he exceeded that total, and in the following year he added another 1.8 million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 舊制，每歲運江淮米五十萬斛抵河陰，久不盈其數，唯巽三年登焉。

translations.literal: By old regulation, each year five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice were transported to Heyin; for a long time the quota was not filled; only Xun in three years achieved it.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai grain were shipped each year to Heyin, a quota long unmet—until Li Xun fulfilled it three years running.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，明年改吏部尚書，使任如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Military Affairs; the next year changed to Minister of Personnel; his commissioner duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Military Affairs, and the following year transferred to Minister of Personnel while retaining his commission unchanged.

sentences.zh: 巽精於吏職，蓋性使然也。

translations.literal: Xun was expert in administrative duties—probably his nature was such.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun excelled at bureaucratic work—it was simply in his nature.

sentences.zh: 雖在私家，亦置案牘簿書，勾檢如公署焉。

translations.literal: Even in private life he also set out dossiers and ledgers, checking accounts like a public office.
translations.idiomatic: Even at home he kept files and ledgers, auditing accounts as though he were still in a government office.

sentences.zh: 人吏有過，絲毫無所貸，雖在千里外，其恐栗如在巽前。

translations.literal: When men and clerks had faults, not the slightest was forgiven; even a thousand li away, they trembled in fear as if before Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He showed subordinates no mercy whatever for any fault. Even a thousand li away they trembled as though he were standing over them.

sentences.zh: 初，程異附王叔文貶竄，巽知其吏才明辯，奏而用之，憲宗不違其請。

translations.literal: At first Cheng Yi, having attached himself to Wang Shuwen, was exiled; Xun knew his clerical talent was clear and eloquent, memorialized and used him; Xianzong did not refuse his request.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi had earlier been exiled for siding with Wang Shuwen, but Li Xun recognized his talent for clear, forceful administration and recommended him for office. Emperor Xianzong granted the request.

sentences.zh: 異勾檢簿籍，又精於巽，故課最加衍，亦異之助焉。

translations.literal: Yi checked ledgers and account books, and was even more expert than Xun; therefore assessment yields increased and expanded—also Yi's assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi audited the books with even greater skill than Li Xun himself, so revenue totals kept climbing—with Cheng Yi's help.

sentences.zh: 巽為吏部尚書，臥疾，郎官相率省問，巽初不言其病，與之考校程課，商略功利，至其夕而卒。

translations.literal: Xun was Minister of Personnel, ill abed; bureau directors successively came to inquire; Xun at first did not speak of his illness, and with them examined schedules and quotas, discussed profit and utility—by that evening he died.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Minister of Personnel, Li Xun fell ill. When bureau directors came in succession to visit, he at first said nothing of his illness and instead reviewed schedules and quotas with them, discussing business until he died that evening.

sentences.zh: 然性強很狡惡，忌刻頗甚，乘德宗之怒，謀殺竇參，物論冤之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was obstinate, cunning, and wicked; his jealousy and harshness were quite severe; riding Dezong's anger, he plotted to kill Dou Can—public opinion deemed it a wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature stubborn, ruthless, and deeply jealous. Exploiting Emperor Dezong's wrath he engineered the death of Dou Can—a killing widely regarded as unjust.

sentences.zh: 初，參為宰相，不悅於巽，自左司郎中出為常州刺史，仍促其行。

translations.literal: At first when Can was chancellor, displeased with Xun, from Director in the Left Bureau he was sent out as Prefect of Changzhou, and his departure was still hurried.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Dou Can was chancellor, Li Xun had fallen out of his favor. Can had him transferred from Director in the Left Bureau to prefect of Changzhou and pressed him to leave at once.

sentences.zh: 不數月，參貶郴州司馬。

translations.literal: Within not many months Can was demoted to Military Aide of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Dou Can himself was demoted to military aide at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，巽自給事中為湖南觀察使，郴即屬郡也。

translations.literal: After a long time, Xun went from Supervising Censor to Hunan Observation Commissioner—Chenzhou was precisely a subordinate prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Li Xun had risen from Supervising Secretariat Drafter to Hunan observation commissioner, Chenzhou fell under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 宣武軍節度使劉士寧以擅襲父任，物議不可，朝廷不得已而授之。

translations.literal: Xuanwu Circuit Military Governor Liu Shining, for seizing his father's post on his own authority, was unacceptable in public opinion; the court had no choice but to appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shining of Xuanwu Circuit had seized his father's command without authorization—a move widely condemned, yet the court had no choice but to confirm the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及參之貶，士寧嘗以絹數千匹賂參，巽在湖南具奏其事，言參與籓鎮交通，德宗怒，遂賜參死，議者冤之。

translations.literal: When Can was demoted, Shining had once bribed Can with several thousand bolts of silk; Xun in Hunan fully memorialized this matter, saying Can communicated with military governors; Dezong was angry, and ordered Can's death; critics deemed it wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can was demoted, Liu Shining had once given him several thousand bolts of silk as a bribe. Reporting from Hunan, Li Xun laid out the full story, accusing Can of trafficking with frontier military governors. Emperor Dezong was enraged and ordered Dou Can executed—a death many considered a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 巽廉察江西，徇喜怒之情，而無罪被戮者多矣。

translations.literal: Xun as investigating commissioner in Jiangxi indulged feelings of favor and anger, and many who were guiltless were executed.
translations.idiomatic: During his inspection tour in Jiangxi, Li Xun indulged his passions—and many innocent people were put to death.

sentences.zh: 元和四年四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Fourth month, fourth year of Yuanhe, he died, age seventy-one; posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of 809, aged seventy-one, and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：歷代操利柄為國計者，莫不損下益上，危人自安，變法以弄權，斂怨以構禍，皆有之矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: In every age those who grasped the profit lever for state planning, without exception harmed the lower to benefit the upper, endangered others to secure themselves, changed laws to wield power, and gathered resentments to bring on calamity—all have had these.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Throughout history, those who held the reins of fiscal power in service of state finance have invariably enriched the throne at the people's expense, endangered others to save themselves, changed the laws to play politics, and stockpiled resentments that bred disaster—all of this has happened before.

sentences.zh: 如劉晏通擁滯，任才能，富其國而不勞於民，儉於家而利於眾。

translations.literal: Such as Liu Yan, who cleared congestion, employed talent and ability, enriched the state without burdening the people, was frugal in his household and beneficial to the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was different: he cleared bottlenecks, put talent to use, enriched the state without overburdening the people, kept his household frugal, and brought benefit to all.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：鄭子產吏不能欺，宓子賤吏不忍欺，西門豹吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Someone asked: "Zi Chan of Zheng—clerks could not deceive him; Mi Zi Jian—clerks could not bear to deceive him; Xi Men Bao—clerks did not dare deceive him."
translations.idiomatic: One might ask: "With Zichan of Zheng, clerks could not cheat him; with Master Fu Ziqian, they could not bear to cheat him; with Ximen Bao, they did not dare cheat him."

sentences.zh: 三子者，古之賢人也，吏皆懷其欺而不能、不忍、不敢也。

translations.literal: These three men were worthy men of antiquity; clerks all harbored deception but could not, could not bear to, and did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: These three were sages of old. Their clerks may have wished to cheat them, but found themselves unable, unwilling, or too afraid.

sentences.zh: 晏之吏，遠近自不欺者何也？

translations.literal: Yan's clerks, near and far, naturally did not deceive—why?
translations.idiomatic: Why was it that Liu Yan's subordinates, near and far, simply did not cheat?

sentences.zh: 答曰：蓋任其才而得其人也。

translations.literal: The answer: Probably because he employed their talents and obtained the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: because he put the right people in the right roles and let them apply their talents.

sentences.zh: 晏歿，故吏二十余年繼掌財賦，不其是哉！

translations.literal: When Yan died, his former clerks for more than twenty years successively managed finance and taxation—is this not proof!
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yan's death, his former subordinates continued to manage the treasury for more than twenty years—is that not proof enough?

sentences.zh: 《史記貨殖》云：「平糶齊物，關市不乏，治國之道也。」

translations.literal: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says: "Evening out grain purchases to equalize goods, markets and passes not lacking—this is the way of governing a state.
translations.idiomatic: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says, "Regulating grain prices to stabilize goods, keeping markets and frontier passes supplied—this is the art of governing.

sentences.zh: 晏治天下，無甚貴甚賤之物，泛言治國者，其可及乎！

translations.literal: Yan governed the realm; there were no extremely expensive or extremely cheap goods; speaking broadly of those who govern states, can they reach this!
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Yan's administration the realm saw neither ruinously high nor ruinously low prices. How many who speak of governing a nation can match that?

sentences.zh: 舉真卿才，忠也，減王縉罪，正也，忠正之道，復出於人，嗚呼！

translations.literal: Recommending Zhenqing's talent was loyalty; reducing Wang Jin's punishment was righteousness; the way of loyalty and righteousness again emerged in a person—alas!
translations.idiomatic: To recommend Yan Zhenqing showed loyalty; to lighten Wang Jin's punishment showed integrity. The virtues of loyalty and righteousness lived again in a single man—alas!

sentences.zh: 本秀於林，風必摧之，常袞見忌於前，楊炎致冤於後，可為長嘆息矣！

translations.literal: Timber outstanding in the forest—wind is sure to break it; Chang Gun envied him earlier; Yang Yan brought wrongful death later—one can only sigh long!
translations.idiomatic: A tree that stands above the forest is sure to be broken by the wind. Chang Gun resented him first; Yang Yan engineered his ruin afterward—enough to draw a long sigh.

sentences.zh: 時譏有口者以利啖之，茍不塞讒口，何以持重權？

translations.literal: At the time slanderers with mouths were fed with profit; if one does not stop slanderous mouths, how can one hold heavy power?
translations.idiomatic: At the time, critics with wagging tongues were bought off with profit. Unless you silenced those tongues, how could you hold real power?

sentences.zh: 即無以展其才，濟其國矣。

translations.literal: Then there is no way to display one's talent and save the state.
translations.idiomatic: Without that, there was no way to deploy one's abilities or serve the nation.

sentences.zh: 是其術也，又何譏焉。

translations.literal: This was his method—what is there to slander?
translations.idiomatic: That was his approach—and what is there to condemn in it?

sentences.zh: 第五琦促辦應卒，民不加賦，而國豐饒，亦庶幾矣。

translations.literal: Fifth Qi rushed preparations to meet emergencies; the people were not increased in taxes, yet the state was abundant—this too nearly succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth Qi mobilized resources swiftly in crisis without raising taxes on the people, and the treasury still grew flush—a feat nearly as admirable.

sentences.zh: 然鑄錢變法，物貴身危，其何陋哉！

translations.literal: Yet casting coins and changing laws made goods expensive and himself endangered—how base!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his recoinage and legal tinkering drove up prices and put his own life at risk—how crude!

sentences.zh: 凡利國者，農商之外，不可為也。

translations.literal: Generally what benefits the state—outside agriculture and commerce—cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, anything that enriches the state beyond agriculture and commerce should not be attempted.

sentences.zh: 宏、滂爭權樹黨，皆非令人。

translations.literal: Hong and Pang fought for power and built factions—neither was a man to be admired.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong and Zhang Pang schemed for power and built factions—neither was a man one could respect.

sentences.zh: 紹之謹密幹事，巽之皦察精辨，亦足可稱。

translations.literal: Shao's discretion in handling affairs, Xun's clear scrutiny and precise discernment—also sufficient to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao's caution and efficiency, Li Xun's sharp-eyed precision—these too deserve recognition.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：豐財忠良，晏道為長。

translations.literal: Eulogy: Abundant wealth and loyal integrity—Yan's way is foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Enriching the treasury through loyal service—Liu Yan's way stands foremost.

sentences.zh: 琦、宏、滂、巽，鹹以利彰。

translations.literal: Qi, Hong, Pang, and Xun—all alike were famed through profit.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth Qi, Ban Hong, Zhang Pang, and Li Xun—all won fame through fiscal mastery.
